owner_rules: Done means ALL evidence: implemented as specified (task id), a test that FAILED before and passes now, suites green, measured number vs target, docs regenerated, committed AND pushed to the contract's branch.
Never defer: no "later", "follow-up", "out of scope". If blocked: what blocks, what you tried, what you need; then continue with the next task.
Root cause, then fix: file:line + mechanism. No weakening tests, raising timeouts, skips, relaxed assertions.
No silent scope cuts: never lower targets, caps or test sizes without owner approval.
Never bypass guards: no --no-verify, no bypass env vars, no skip flags.
Deliver continuously: one task per commit, pushed to the contract's branch as it goes green.
Honest reporting: TASK-ID | status | commit | tests | measured vs target | missing.

tasks.title: Log-first holds for writes
requirements: on open, a path whose last logged put is newer than the file on disk and whose file content equals the put's previous head is completed from the log, not imported as external
a file that differs from both the logged head and the previous head is still imported as an external edit, so a real outside edit is never lost
README and DESIGN.md state log-first for writes and appends
the doctor's drift message and its fix describe log-first completion, not an import of the old file, and the fix never writes the old body over a logged newer one
recover() runs only in an open that holds the SR-1.01 vault lock; .memev/daemon.lock plays no part in that decision, and a read-only open never recovers

write() and append() build their record from the logged head, not from the file on disk: the diff, the splice base and the append hash start from the head's content, so a call made while a logged change is still pending logs on top of it; when the file on disk does not equal the head, the call's file step writes the full new content (the head with this change applied) through a temporary file and a rename, never an append to the stale file

a file that is a strict prefix of the logged content, other than a file equal to the previous head and older than the put (requirement 1 completes that one), is completed only when it starts with the previous head and the last record for the path is an append; any other shorter file is an outside edit and is imported; recovery writes a completed file through a temporary file, an fsync and a rename, so an interrupted completion leaves the old file or the new one

a file is torn only when the bytes before its first NUL are a prefix of the logged head or the previous head and every byte from there on is NUL, whatever its length, and a torn file is completed from the log; any other file, a UTF-16 save or invalid UTF-8 included, is an outside edit and its bytes on disk are kept
a completion that fails (EACCES, EPERM, EIO, ENOSPC) leaves the path pending with its reason recorded and never makes Vault.open() throw

on open, every path that recovery completed, and every path whose index entry is older than its head, is reindexed; index.jsonl records the log seq it reflects, so a stale index is brought up to date rather than trusted; with git enabled, open queues a commit for every note whose file equals its head but differs from the committed copy

a logged delete whose file is still on disk with an mtime older than the delete record is completed (the file removed); a newer file is a real outside edit and is imported; syncFromDisk on such a path completes the delete instead of importing the file

when a write or append is logged but its file step fails, the call throws a VaultError with code logged_pending that carries the logged seq, so a caller knows the change is durable and does not repeat it

completion from the log applies only while the file still holds what the pending change was logged against (the previous head, a prefix of the logged content, or a torn file); a file edited during the pending window is an outside edit, imported before the next call logs
write(), append() and recovery fsync the temporary file before the rename when fsync is on, and never open the note path itself for writing
a completion that fails for any reason (EACCES, EPERM, ENOSPC, EIO or another) leaves the path pending with its error code recorded
the MCP and HTTP error paths carry logged_pending's seq and tell the caller not to repeat the call, and memev_remember reports a duplicate for an entry whose append threw logged_pending
the doctor's drift fix completes only paths awaiting completion; a note edited by hand is imported as an outside edit, never overwritten

criteria.statement: c21 a non-UTF-8 outside edit is never destroyed (command guard: base already passes). Write B successfully and close. By hand replace the file with Latin-1 bytes (for example Buffer.from('caf' + String.fromCharCode(0xe9) + ' edited by hand', 'latin1')) with its mtime 10 s after the put.
